strategyPoints: With such a short lap on the Curvelo Short Circuit, traffic management will be crucial during the race. Overtaking opportunities are limited.
Tire wear will be a significant factor on this abrasive surface, even on the shorter layout. Managing the tires will be key to a good result.
The pit window will be relatively short on this 1.8km circuit, so teams will need to be precise with their timing.
Fuel consumption will be less of a concern than on the full circuit, but teams still need to ensure they have enough to reach the finish.
With the short lap time, the undercut could be a very powerful strategy here. A well-timed pit stop could gain a driver several positions.
The emphasis is on mechanical grip here. Teams will be looking for a setup that allows the drivers to attack the corners without overheating the tires.
A safety car period on this short circuit would bunch the field up, creating a potential for late-race drama. Teams need to be ready to react.
The reduced lap length means more laps overall, increasing the chances of incidents and strategic variations.
weatherCommentary: The Brazilian climate can be unpredictable, and a sudden downpour could completely change the complexion of the race here at Curvelo.
The heat is intense today, which will put a strain on both the drivers and their cars. Hydration will be key.

The high altitude here in Curvelo can affect engine performance, so teams will need to adjust their engine maps accordingly.
The humidity is always a factor in Brazil, making it even more challenging for the drivers inside the cockpit.
